elements.label: Figure 6.1
elements.description:
Two stacked bar charts (panels 2010 and 2020) showing the share of households (%) by expenditure decile, with bars split into 'Same' (teal) and 'Worsened' (orange). X-axis: deciles 1 (=poorest) to 10 (=richest). Y-axis: 'Share of households (%)'. Values are not printed; approximate readings follow.

2010 panel (y-axis 0–30, ticks every 5): total / Same / Worsened
- 1: ~28 / ~20 / ~8
- 2: ~24 / ~15.5 / ~8.5
- 3: ~18.5 / ~11.5 / ~7
- 4: ~18 / ~11 / ~7
- 5: ~16.5 / ~11 / ~5.5
- 6: ~15 / ~9.3 / ~5.7
- 7: ~14.3 / ~9.2 / ~5.1
- 8: ~14 / ~8.8 / ~5.2
- 9: ~10.7 / ~7.1 / ~3.6
- 10: ~9.5 / ~7.1 / ~2.4

2020 panel (y-axis 0–25, ticks every 5): total / Same / Worsened
- 1: ~22 / ~14 / ~8
- 2: ~18.7 / ~11.2 / ~7.5
- 3: ~16.4 / ~9.3 / ~7.1
- 4: ~13.5 / ~8.9 / ~4.6
- 5: ~10.6 / ~6 / ~4.6
- 6: ~12.7 / ~5.6 / ~7.1
- 7: ~10.3 / ~4.8 / ~5.5
- 8: ~15 / ~8.5 / ~6.5
- 9: ~11.8 / ~6.8 / ~5
- 10: ~10 / ~5 / ~5

Pattern: the share reporting worsened or same conditions is highest among the poorest deciles and declines toward the richest deciles in both years; the 'Same' segment is the largest part of each bar, and the 2020 totals are generally lower than 2010 for the poorest groups.
